drug_class: Combination antidiabetic agent — long-acting insulin plus GLP-1 receptor agonist
purpose: This medication is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines two medicines in one injection to make managing your diabetes easier. It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range.
how_it_works: This medicine contains two ingredients that work together. Insulin degludec is a long-acting insulin that helps lower your blood sugar by allowing sugar to move from your blood into your body's cells for energy. Liraglutide helps your pancreas release insulin when you eat, slows down digestion so sugar enters your blood more slowly, and also helps reduce your appetite — all of which help keep your blood sugar steady throughout the day.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, headache, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or itching. Nausea is usually mild and often gets better after the first few weeks of treatment.
warnings: This medicine comes with a serious warning about a rare but potentially life-threatening type of thyroid tumor seen in animal studies, so it should not be used if you or a family member has had certain thyroid cancers or a condition called MEN 2. It should not be used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Watch for signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, dizziness, or confusion and treat it right away. Tell your doctor if you have a history of pancreatitis, kidney problems, or severe stomach issues.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as one injection under the skin (usually in your stomach, thigh, or upper arm) once a day at the same time each day. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and gradually increase it based on how your blood sugar is responding. The dose is measured in units using a special pen device — never mix it with other insulins. Do not share your pen with anyone else.
